ageing_relevance.rationale: High ageing/senescence literature share, UniProt links to cellular senescence, associations with several age-related diseases, and it is a GrimAge component. The GrimAge surrogate is a methylation estimate, not measured protein.

evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up GrimAge, the mortality clock that was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia in part 1 of this project (an effect explained by smoking). The surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels. Shirai et al. 2024 (7-cohort meta-analysis): DNAm-predicted level higher in schizophrenia/first-episode psychosis.

background_knowledge: Human PAI-1 deficiency is associated with longevity in Amish carriers (Khan et al. 2017); PAI-1 inhibition extends lifespan in progeroid mouse models.

mechanism.rationale: Well-characterised inhibitor of tPA/uPA with a defined role in fibrinolysis and senescence. Lowering activity is the likely direction, though the senescence mechanism is less fully resolved.

evidence.value: Serine protease inhibitor. Inhibits TMPRSS7 (PubMed:15853774). Is a primary inhibitor of tissue-type plasminogen activator (PLAT) and urokinase-type plasminogen activator (PLAU).
It is involved in cellular and replicative senescence (PubMed:16862142).

tractability.rationale: Small-molecule tractability is strong (advanced clinical, ligand-bound structure, high-quality pocket). An antibody is feasible since the protein is secreted. A PROTAC is less relevant for a secreted target. No approved drug.

safety.rationale: Open Targets lists two liabilities (osteonecrosis, gene expression regulation). Congenital deficiency is linked to abnormal bleeding, so inhibition carries a bleeding risk. Antifibrinolytic biology is well understood.

value: congenital plasminogen activator inhibitor type 1 deficiency (0.684)

background_knowledge: Human PAI-1 deficiency causes a mild-to-moderate bleeding diathesis.

clinical_precedence.rationale: Only one drug has reached the clinic, aleplasinin, which reached Phase 1. There is no later-stage or approved drug.

assessment.summary: SERPINE1 (PAI-1) is a secreted inhibitor of tPA/uPA with a documented role in cellular senescence. It has a high ageing literature share (about 21%) and is linked to several age-related diseases (coronary artery disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes, Alzheimer disease). It is also a GrimAge component. It is tractable by small molecule and antibody, but the only clinical drug, aleplasinin, stopped at Phase 1. The main risk is bleeding from reduced PAI-1 activity. We would inhibit it, and I recommend prioritising it, with caution about the bleeding window.
key_uncertainties: Bleeding risk with chronic PAI-1 inhibition in older people
The GrimAge link is a DNAm surrogate, not measured protein, and the schizophrenia elevation is explained by smoking
Whether PAI-1 is causal in human ageing or only a marker of inflammation and metabolic state
Why clinical development stalled at Phase 1
